newsitem.title: DENMARK: CSFB sees flatter Danish 10/30 yr yield curve.
newsitem.headline: CSFB sees flatter Danish 10/30 yr yield curve.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) investment bank said it forecast a continued flattening in the 10/30 year bond segment in Denmark, with the spread still lagging Germany and France.

"The yield gap between 10- and 30-year Danish state bonds has also narrowed considerably and we still see some potential in 10/30 trade," CSFB said in its latest Nordic Weekly Report, received on Thursday.
The spread between the two was 86 basis points on Thursday, compared with more than 100 one month ago.
CSFB said it saw the differential narrowing further to 75 basis points in the coming months.

It also said it recommended the six percent Danish mortgage credit bond due 2026 as a substitute for the Danish state bond in the 10-year spread versus Germany, with the 10-year yield gap between Denmark and Germany now just below 50 basis points.
"This construction would make the trade more robust towards global setbacks," CSFB said.

The spread between the Danish eight percent 2006 benchmark and the 2026 mortgage paper was 111 basis points on Thursday and CSFB said it remained positive on prospects for narrowing of this spread. --Per Bech Thomsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969656
